prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "dalledress", with the standing line "Turns a short seed phrase into a reproducible image prompt by drawing words from embedded databases, then renders and annotates the picture." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A paper slip reading "Person Tour Coordinates" enters at top left. An arrow carries it down into a tall chest of nineteen shallow drawers, which are the word databases. A perforated stencil lies across the drawer fronts and leaves only some openings clear; this is the chosen Series. One small card is pulled from each open drawer. The cards slide right and gather onto a single prompt sheet. An arrow runs from the sheet to a distant image provider. A finished picture returns and travels on toward .

Magnified circles set beside it show circle one shows the seed slip becoming a fixed seed hash, with one image per series. Circle two shows series.tar.gz sealed inside the app, with a padlock on a Built-in series. Circle three shows a user-series folder laid over a built-in of the same name, shadowing it. has four studies: a Model selector, a Background swatch, an Enhance prompt switch rewriting the sheet, and a Generate image switch that sends the prompt away.

Colour is used so that Vermilion marks the seed and everything it determines: the slip, the hash, and the pulled cards. Slate blue marks series: the stencil, the padlock, and the folders. Muted green marks finished artifacts and the completed phase.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 19 word databases, counted on the drawer chest. 13 series filter fields, marked along the stencil edge. 7 working phases, ticked along the foot track. 2 image artifacts, Generated and Annotated, bracketed in .

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: "seed" sits on the paper slip. "Series" sits on the stencil. "adjectives", "nouns", "emotions", "artstyles" and "viewpoints" sit on individual drawer fronts. "prompt" sits on the gathered sheet. "Built-in" sits on the padlock. "series.tar.gz" sits on the sealed archive. "user-series" sits on the overlaid folder. "Enhance prompt", "Generate image", "Background" and "Model" sit on their controls. "Generated" and "Annotated" sit on the two output pictures. "selected records" sits on the small table beside them. "Export Text" sits on the text files. "setup", "base prompts", "enhance", "image prep", "image wait", "image download", "annotate" and "completed" sit on the foot track, in that order.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: Person Tour Coordinates, Series, adjectives, nouns, emotions, artstyles, viewpoints, prompt, image provider seed hash, series.tar.gz, user-series, Built-in Model, Background, Enhance prompt, Generate image Generated, Annotated, title, selected records, Export Text setup, base prompts, enhance, image prep, image wait, image download, annotate, completed

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Records are drawn from the word databases; the series narrows which words may appear. The same seed gives one image per series; built-in series are read-only. Every image keeps its selected records; regenerating rebuilds the image from scratch. A cache hit reuses earlier image artifacts; annotate runs only after an image exists.
